events.title: Palaver Strings: What Travels
events.description:
Palaver Strings presents “What Travels,” a program which will explore the ways memory and knowledge are carried across generations through families, and through music itself.

The concert is set for Sunday, December 6, at 3 p.m. at the BMC.

Among the works performed are Jessie Montgomery’s Source Code, which traces musical lineages and inherited ideas, showing how fragments of the past help shape new creation. Flowing directly into Osvaldo Golijov’s Tenebrae, the music takes the audience to a place of grief, stillness, and remembrance. Continuing with Diego Vega Desenne’s Diaspora, the pieces expand outward to explore themes of migration, displacement, and resilience through the musical traditions of Latin America.

Together, these three works consider what endures as people move, traditions evolve, and what travels across borders and through time. In the end, “What Travels” affirms that music itself is one of humanity’s most enduring forms of memory.

events.title: Windborne’s Music of Midwinter
events.description:
Celebrate the season with Windborne’s “Music of Midwinter” Thursday, December 10 at 7 p.m. at the BMC.

A joyful and heartfelt celebration of song, Windborne’s lush vocals and unique arrangements bring light to a dark time, drawing on midwinter music from traditional, classical, and folk roots in the U.S., British Isles and beyond.

The audience will be delighted by holiday stories, songs, and humor in an evening that is sure to become a holiday tradition for the whole family. Sing along with familiar favorites, enjoy new twists on old classics or sit back and enjoy discovering new favorites.

Windborne includes Lauren Breunig and Lynn Mahoney Rowan, vocals; and Jeremy Carter-Gordon and Will Thomas Rowan, vocals and banjo.

events.title: Brattleboro Camerata: The Angel of Great Counsel, Music of Thomas Tallis
events.description:
Camerata, from the Latin for “chamber”, is a term often used to refer to smaller ensembles that specialize in the intimate and virtuosic genre of chamber music, usually from earlier eras. The Brattleboro Camerata is just such a group – a chamber vocal ensemble devoted to exploring the craft, beauty, and transcendence of the music of the European Renaissance.

Camerata’s performances breathe life anew into ancient music, enveloping the listener in the astonishing sonic geometry of Renaissance Polyphony.

events.title: Tessitura: David Lang, Poor Hymnal
events.description:
Tessitura is a chamber choir which explores music of the Baroque and modern eras. Its repertoire ranges from Monteverdi madrigals to Bach cantatas; from motets of Schütz to works by contemporary composers. The 2025-2026 season featured Book Six of Monteverdi’s Madrigals, Poulenc’s Four Motets in a Time of Penitence, Paul Mealor’s “She Walks in Beauty,” the Kyrie from Fenno Heath’s Mass, and Eric Whitacre’s “Sleep.”

“Tessitura” is the most resonant part of one’s vocal range; the term is also the Italian word for weaving—and thus by extension suggests the interplay among disparate threads to effect modulations of texture. Under the direction of Mark Nelson, this ensemble illuminates the shifting colors and textures suffusing old and new music.

events.title: Chamber Series: Sound Ritual – Catalyst
events.description:
Created by DeShaun Gordon-King’s Sound Ritual is an immersive musical experience that brings together therapeutic music, chamber music, jazz and improvisation, electronics, and guided meditation to create a shared space for reflection, restoration, and connection. Drawing inspiration from traditions of sound medicine alongside contemporary musical practice, the performance invites audiences into an environment of deep listening where music becomes both artistic expression and communal ritual.

 

Created in response to the loneliness and isolation brought into sharp focus during the COVID-19 pandemic, DeShaun Gordon-King’s Sound Ritual explores music’s capacity to foster presence, belonging, and connection. Through an expansive sonic landscape, the experience invites audiences to reconnect with themselves, one another, and the possibility of imagining a more compassionate and connected world.

The result is an immersive experience where listening itself becomes a practice of presence, restoration, and shared humanity.

The Brattleboro Camerata is a chamber choir devoted to exploring the beauty and

performances breathe new life into old music, bringing vivid and expressive intensity to
innovative thematic programs that highlight canonic favorites, under-performed gems by
neglected voices, and new works that allow us to see early music in a different light.
With Music Director Timothy Parsons, the Camerata endeavors to ensure that early
music continues as a vibrant, living tradition.

events.title: In Stile Moderno
events.description:
In Stile Moderno is an ensemble for early music, founded in Basel, Switzerland in 2012 by soprano Agnes Coakley and lutenist/cornettist Nathaniel Cox. Named after the “modern style” of music which emerged in Italy around 1600, the ensemble is dedicated to music of the seventeenth century, and combines fidelity to historical performance practice with a drive to make early music accessible and relevant to modern audiences. Both as a lute and voice duo and in larger formations with cornetto, organ, voice, and plucked instruments, In Stile Moderno has charmed audiences with their engaging performances of seventeenth-century music in Boston, Vermont, and New York, as well as in concert series in Switzerland, Germany, and France.
